label: Trust Infrastructure Schemas Binding
description: Binds TSMM semantic concepts to executable Trust Infrastructure Schemas artifacts for authority, evidence, evaluation, decision, registry, assurance, and artifact references.

guarantees.name: layer-boundary
guarantees.description: TSMM concepts are projected into TIS artifacts without transferring semantic ownership of the core model.

guarantees.name: decision-interoperability
guarantees.description: TSMM runtime decisions can be represented as TIS decision receipts with explicit authority, policy, evidence, result, and timestamp fields.

guarantees.name: assurance-crosswalk
guarantees.description: TSMM profile postures map to TIS AL1-AL4 as guidance. Agentic is a risk context, not an assurance level.

limitations.name: not-a-conformance-claim
limitations.impact: Binding use does not certify an implementation as conformant to either repository.
limitations.mitigation: Use repo validation scripts and release-specific conformance declarations.

limitations.name: lossless-transform-not-guaranteed
limitations.impact: Some TSMM graph semantics may require references or extensions when projected into a flat artifact.
limitations.mitigation: Preserve TSMM node and edge references in TIS semantic_bindings or artifact metadata.

behavioralExpectations.expectation: A TIS artifact SHOULD cite the TSMM concept, node, edge, or receipt from which it was derived.
Discovery or publication MUST NOT be interpreted as runtime authorization.
Runtime reliance SHOULD record revocation status checks in decision receipts or authority boundaries.

mappings.description: A TIS authority boundary is an artifact-level projection of a TSMM authority node or edge.
TIS packages TSMM EvidenceArtifact references for validation and audit.
Evaluation envelopes capture verifier assessment evidence and assurance result.
TIS decision receipts are executable records of TSMM trust decisions and operational effects.
TIS registry entries publish discoverable trust state but do not authorize runtime effects.
TSMM profile language is contextual; TIS AL values express assurance rigor.
Policy references bind a decision to external rules without embedding all policy logic.
TIS result constraints represent the operational effect of a trust decision.

notes: This binding is intentionally additive and does not replace existing TRQP, OASF, ODRL, A2A, or GTR bindings.
TIS schemas provide executable artifact contracts; TSMM provides semantic interpretation and graph-level interoperability.
Use with validation scripts and explicit profile declarations.
